arxiv-2104-14814.title: Dbar-approach to coupled nonlocal NLS equation and general nonlocal Reduction
arxiv-2104-14814.creator: Xueru Wang, Junyi Zhu
arxiv-2104-14814.description: Abstract The coupled nonlocal NLS equation is studied by virtue of the 2 × 2 2\times 2 Dbar-problem. Two spectral transform matrices are introduced to define two associated Dbar-problems. The relations between the coupled nonlocal NLS potential and the solution of the Dbar-problem are constructed.

arxiv-2211-06117.title: Closed-Form Global Optimization of Beyond Diagonal Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces Thanks: This work was supported by Hong Kong Research Grants Council through the Collaborative Research Fund under Grant C6012-20G. ( Corresponding author: Shanpu Shen .) Thanks: M. Nerini is with the Department o
arxiv-2211-06117.creator: Matteo Nerini, Shanpu Shen
arxiv-2211-06117.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Matteo Nerini, Shanpu Shen. Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) allow controlling the propagation environment in wireless networks by tuning multiple reflecting elements. RISs have been traditionally realized through single connected architectures, mathematically characterized by a diagonal scattering matrix. Recently, beyond diagonal RISs (BD-RISs) have been proposed as a novel branch of RISs whose scattering matrix is not limited to be diagonal, which creates new benefits and opportunities for RISs. Efficient BD-RIS architectures have been realized based on group and fully connected reconfigurable impedance networks.

arxiv-2212-02420.title: Scaling of secondary flows with surface parameters: a linear approach
arxiv-2212-02420.creator: Gerardo Zampino, Davide Lasagna, Bharathram Ganapathisubramani
arxiv-2212-02420.description: Abstract Secondary flows are generated when a lateral variation of the topography, such as streamwise aligned ridges, is imposed to a turbulent wall-bounded flow. In this case, the flow field is characterized by vortical structures developing along the streamwise direction known as Prandt’s vortices of the second kind ( Prandtl 1952 ) .

arxiv-2306-11475.title: Delegated Classification
arxiv-2306-11475.creator: Eden Saig, Inbal Talgam-Cohen, Nir Rosenfeld Technion – Israel Institute of Technology Haifa, Israel {edens,italgam,nirr}@cs.technion.ac.il
arxiv-2306-11475.description: Abstract When machine learning is outsourced to a rational agent, conflicts of interest might arise and severely impact predictive performance. In this work, we propose a theoretical framework for incentive-aware delegation of machine learning tasks. We model delegation as a principal-agent game, in which accurate learning can be incentivized by the principal using performance-based contracts.

arxiv-2406-06128.title: Federated Machine Reasoning for Resource Provisioning in 6G O-RAN
arxiv-2406-06128.creator: Swastika Roy, Hatim Chergui, Adlen Ksentini, Christos Verikoukis
arxiv-2406-06128.description: Abstract O-RAN specifications reshape RANs with function disaggregation and open interfaces, driven by RAN Intelligent Controllers. This enables data-driven management through AI/ML but poses trust challenges due to human operators’ limited understanding of AI/ML decision-making. Balancing resource provisioning and avoiding overprovisioning and underprovisioning is critical, especially among the multiple virtualized base station(vBS) instances.

arxiv-2511-14733.title: Starlight-driven flared-staircase geometry in radiation hydrodynamic models of protoplanetary disks

arxiv-2511-14733.description: Abstract Context. Protoplanetary disks observed in millimeter continuum and scattered light show a variety of substructures. While embedded planets are a common explanation, during the early planet formation phase, various physical processes in the disk could also trigger such features.

arxiv-2601-13264.title: Unlearning in LLMs: Methods, Evaluation, and Open Challenges
arxiv-2601-13264.creator: Tyler Lizzo, Larry Heck
arxiv-2601-13264.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success across natural language processing tasks, yet their widespread deployment raises pressing concerns around privacy, copyright, security, and bias. Machine unlearning has emerged as a promising paradigm for selectively removing knowledge or data from trained models without full retraining.

pmc-10712193.creator: Harri Hemilä, Elizabeth Chalker
pmc-10712193.description: BackgroundRandomized trials have shown that vitamin C shortens the duration of common colds. pmc-11669597.title: School absenteeism as a predictor of functional gastrointestinal disorders in children
pmc-11669597.creator: Seth M. Tersteeg, Stephen M. Borowitz
pmc-11669597.description: IntroductionChronic abdominal complaints are common in school-aged children. pmc-12682085.title: Long-term test and retest reliability of clinical vergence testing
pmc-12682085.creator: Mitchell Scheiman, Aparna Raghuram, Christina Master, Matthew L Robich, Andrew Toole, Erica R Shelton, Gayathri Srinivasan, Sophia Marusic, Siva Meiyeppen, Lisa A Jordan, Tawna L Roberts, EPICC Study Group
pmc-12682085.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). PurposeTo establish long-term reliability measures for vergence testing in a control population of adolescents.MethodsHealthy participants between 12 and 17.5 years with normal binocular vision were recruited from 10 clinical sites. Cover test, near point of convergence (NPC), positive and negative fusional vergences, vergence facility (12∆ base-out/3∆ base-in) and vergence jumps (using the Oculomotor Assessment Tool) were performed at the initial visit and repeated at 90 days.

pmc-13290432.title: Influenza Antiviral Prescriptions in the US Inpatient and Outpatient Settings During the 2015–2022 Influenza Seasons
pmc-13290432.creator: Kyueun Lee, Anirban Basu, Janet A Englund
pmc-13290432.description: BackgroundsThe antiviral drug prescription landscape has changed as new antivirals for influenza treatment have been approved. Understanding this landscape is important to assess potential under‐ and mis‐utilization and to address gaps in care. This study characterizes patterns in influenza antiviral use in US healthcare settings using a large claims database.

pmc-13586588.title: GV21 enables ultrasound molecular imaging of tumor cell-associated VEGFR2 for early therapy assessment
pmc-13586588.creator: Xiaoxin Liang, Shilin Lu, Liang Yang, Jianhua Zhou, Fei Yan
pmc-13586588.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (VEGFR2) plays a crucial role in tumor growth through accelerating tumor angiogenesis. Recently, increasing evidence indicates that VEGFR2 is also overexpressed on tumor cells in multiple cancers, contributing to tumor progression and survival. BR55, a kind of VEGFR2-targeted microbubbles, has been developed and exhibited a promising potential for ultrasound molecular imaging (USMI) of early-stage tumors.

uslaw-usc-t12-s623.title: 12 U.S.C. § 623 — Voluntary liquidation
uslaw-usc-t12-s623.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t12-s623.description: United States Code, Title 12 (Banks And Banking); Chapter 6 (Foreign Banking); Subchapter II (Organization Of Corporations To Do Foreign Banking). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Any corporation organized under this subchapter may go into voluntary liquidation and be closed by a vote of its shareholders owning two-thirds of its stock.
